newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria said to delay call for CA bids.
newsitem.headline: Austria said to delay call for CA bids.

text.p: Austria will delay a call for bids for the nation's second biggest bank Creditanstalt Bankverein until the end of next week or the beginning of the following week, sources close to Creditanstalt said on Friday.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima had planned to restart the bank's privatisation by the end of this week. No one at the finance ministry was immediately available for comment.

Austria has been trying to off-load its 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary voting shares for over five years. In September it turned down the only firm bid from an international consortium led by insurer EA-Generali.
Then the finance ministry said U.S. investment house JP Morgan would update a study of the bank by the end of this week. There would then be a four to six-week bidding period.
At current market prices the government's 19.9 million shares are worth almost 14 billion schillings.
Creditanstalt chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari reiterated on Friday that he hoped the saga would soon draw to an end.
"I am extremely interested in seeing the matter cleared up," he said during an investors' fair.
